name: broccoli
answer: Yes, at a standard serve. Monash rates 75 g of whole broccoli (about ¾ cup) low. The heads are the gentler part; the stalks hold most of the excess fructose, so keep large servings of stalks alone small.

servings.note: Low amount from Monash; the moderate amount is as reported by Karlijn's Kitchen from Monash's data.
Grams as reported by Karlijn's Kitchen from Monash's data. Monash's own post says to avoid more than 65 g of stalks alone if fructose bothers you.

changes.text: Monash retested broccoli and split it into heads and stalks. Excess fructose, mostly in the stalks, turned out to be the main FODMAP.

disagreements.text: Monash calls whole broccoli and heads low at a typical 1 cup serve, but doesn't give that cup in grams. Elsewhere it lists 75 g as about ¾ cup, so a full cup is likely more than 75 g.

notes.text: Broccolini is the opposite of broccoli: its FODMAPs sit mostly in the heads, and its stalks are the lower part.
In 2024 Monash lowered its fructose cut-off for vegetables, which shrank the low serve of broccolini heads from 58 g to 21 g.

faq.a: Only in small amounts. The stalks carry most of broccoli's excess fructose, so use mostly florets or mix in whole broccoli.
No lab result for frozen broccoli was found in public sources. Weigh it like fresh broccoli and stick to the standard serve.

name: corn
answer: In small amounts. Monash rates half a cob of fresh sweet corn (38 g) low, while a whole cob is high, mainly from the polyol sorbitol. Canned corn kernels go further: Monash lists 75 g as a low serve.

servings.form: fresh sweet corn on the cob
servings.note: The moderate amount is as reported by Karlijn's Kitchen from Monash's data. Monash says a whole cob is high.
Monash's shopping list says "corn kernels" without naming canned or fresh; Karlijn's Kitchen gives 75 g for canned kernels and the moderate amount.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly agrees a whole cob is high in sorbitol and says canned kernels are low only in small serves, turning high in larger ones.

notes.text: Corn grown for flour has less sorbitol and more starch, so corn tortillas, polenta and cornflour are a different story from sweet corn.
Monash points out that sweet corn shows red at a full cob but green at half a cob, a good example of why serve size matters.

faq.a: Popcorn is a separate food from sweet corn. Monash's fibre guide lists plain commercial popcorn with a low serve; check the pack size and flavourings.
Corn flour has far less sorbitol than sweet corn, so plain corn tortillas are usually a lower-FODMAP choice. Check labels for onion or garlic.

name: tomatoes
answer: In small amounts. About half a medium tomato (65 g) is reported low, and 75 g is moderate in fructose. Monash rates 3 cherry tomatoes (45 g) low and lists canned tomato as low at 75 g.

servings.note: Grams as reported by dietitian sites from Monash's data.
Low amount from Monash; the moderate amount (4 cherry tomatoes) is as reported by Karlijn's Kitchen.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly calls fresh tomatoes low and says they can be eaten freely, while Monash's Step 1 sheet lists tomato among higher-FODMAP foods.

For canned tomatoes, dietitian sites citing Monash give ½ cup (100 g) as the low serve, larger than the 75 g on Monash's shopping list. They also say moderate starts at 115 g or 132 g, depending on the site.

notes.text: FODMAP Friendly found canned tomatoes higher in fructose than fresh, with a low serve of about ⅗ cup.
A whole 400 g can split four ways keeps each plate near the low serve.

faq.a: Plain tomato is fine in small amounts, but many pasta sauces add garlic and onion, which are high. Make your own with canned tomato and garlic-infused oil.
Yes, at about 3 cherry tomatoes per meal. More than that adds up in fructose.

name: potatoes
answer: Yes. Monash rates a standard 75 g serve of potato (half a medium) low and says potato stays low however much you eat. Dietitian sites report Monash's app shows potatoes low up to 500 g.

servings.note: Monash says potato is low regardless of amount; 75 g is the standard serve, not a limit. The sources name no FODMAP that rises with the amount; fructans is shown only as a placeholder.

notes.text: Dietitian sites citing Monash's app report white, red and purple potatoes as low up to 500 g, the largest amount tested.
Monash suggests potato as a bulking vegetable to stretch higher-FODMAP foods, such as in sweet potato soup.

faq.a: Potato itself is. Watch the extras: use lactose-free milk or butter, and skip onion or garlic powder.
Plain potato fries are fine. Check seasonings on store-bought fries, which can include onion or garlic.

name: cabbage
answer: Yes, at a standard serve. Monash lists 75 g of white (common) cabbage as low. Bigger servings are reported to turn moderate in sorbitol from about 100 g. Savoy cabbage was retested in 2025 and is now low at 75 g too.

servings.note: Low amount from Monash; the moderate amount is as reported by Karlijn's Kitchen from Monash's data.
Monash rates it low at 1 serve, which it defines as 75 g of vegetable; it contains fructans in larger serves.

changes.text: Monash retested savoy cabbage: it moved from high in fructans to low at a standard serve. Older dietitian pages still show only 40 g as low.

notes.text: Fermenting changes cabbage: Monash found 1 cup of raw cabbage low but the same amount as sauerkraut high in mannitol.
Even at a low serve, savoy cabbage can still cause wind for some people, Monash says, because of parts of the plant that aren't FODMAPs.

faq.a: The cabbage is fine at a standard serve. Many coleslaw dressings add onion or garlic, so check the label or make your own.
Not in a full cup: Monash found fermented cabbage high in mannitol. Only a small serving is listed as low.

name: carrots
answer: Yes. Monash rates one medium carrot (75 g) low and names carrot as a vegetable with no upper limit, so it stays low in large serves. Dietitian sites report Monash's app shows carrots low up to 500 g.

servings.note: Monash says carrot has no upper limit; 75 g is the standard serve, not a limit. The sources name no FODMAP that rises with the amount; fructans is shown only as a placeholder.

notes.text: George Eats, citing Monash, reports carrots low up to 500 g per person as of August 2026.
Monash uses carrot to bulk out dishes built on foods with tighter limits, such as sweet potato.

faq.a: The carrots are fine. Regular carrot cake uses wheat flour and often raisins, so look for a recipe with low FODMAP flour.
No public lab result for carrot juice was found. Whole carrots are the tested form.

name: green beans
answer: Yes, at a standard serve. Monash rates 15 green beans (75 g) low. Dietitian sites citing Monash report that 25 beans (125 g) carry a moderate amount of sorbitol, so pair them with other vegetables for a bigger plate.

servings.note: Low amount from Monash; the moderate amount is as reported by A Little Bit Yummy from Monash's data.

notes.text: Green beans appear on Monash's shopping list of low FODMAP vegetables at a 75 g serve.

faq.q: Is green bean casserole low FODMAP?
faq.a: The beans are fine at 15 per serve, but classic casseroles use onion and canned soup. A version with garlic-infused oil and lactose-free milk keeps it lower.

faq.q: Are green beans legumes high in GOS like other beans?
faq.a: Fresh green beans are eaten as a pod vegetable; the FODMAP reported in larger serves is sorbitol, not GOS.

name: mushrooms
answer: Mostly no. Fresh button mushrooms are high in mannitol, with only about 7 g reported as low. Oyster mushrooms are the exception: Monash lists 75 g as a low serve. Canned button mushrooms are reported low at 75 g.

servings.note: Grams as reported by Karlijn's Kitchen from Monash's data (Jan 2024). Monash lists button mushroom as a high FODMAP food.
Karlijn's Kitchen reports that Monash gives no upper limit for oyster mushrooms.

servings.form: canned button mushrooms in brine, drained
servings.note: Grams as reported by dietitian sites from Monash's data.

changes.text: Monash's retest found button mushrooms contain fructans as well as mannitol in larger serves, so it dropped them as the mannitol test food in favour of portobello.

disagreements.text: For canned button mushrooms, Karlijn's Kitchen reports 75 g (1 cup), while A Little Bit Yummy reports a serve of 6 mushrooms.

notes.text: Monash names mushrooms as one of the vegetables richest in mannitol.
In a 2026 Monash lab study, microwaving mushrooms in water for 3 minutes and draining them cut their FODMAPs by 58%, but not enough to make them low.
FODMAP Friendly also found many mushroom types high in mannitol, with shimeji much lower than shiitake or enoki.

faq.a: No. Monash now uses portobello as its food for testing mannitol, because it contains mannitol and no other FODMAPs.

faq.q: Are canned mushrooms lower in FODMAPs than fresh?
faq.a: Yes. Canning leaches water-soluble FODMAPs into the brine, so drained canned button mushrooms are reported low at a standard serve.

name: peas
answer: Green peas: no, not at a standard serve. Monash's 2025 retest rated 75 g of frozen green peas high in fructans. Sugar snap peas are different: Monash now rates a standard 75 g serve low.

servings.note: Rated high at 1 serve (75 g), mainly fructans with trace GOS. Monash's public pages give no low amount for green peas.
Low at 1 serve (75 g); contains fructans in larger serves.

changes.text: Monash retested frozen green peas (still high, now mainly fructans rather than GOS) and sugar snap peas (from high in fructose to low at a standard serve).
Snow peas sit on Monash's low FODMAP shopping list at a 75 g serve. In 2015 Monash had listed only 5 pods (16 g) as low.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen, citing Monash, lists canned peas as low up to 54 g. We found no public Monash figure for canned peas.

notes.text: Monash's Step 1 sheet lists green peas among the higher-FODMAP vegetables to swap out.
FODMAP Friendly's public food list puts peas on the high side too.

faq.a: Monash's 2025 shopping list includes snow peas at a standard 75 g serve.
Pea protein isolate is a separate product from whole peas, so the pea results here don't apply to it. Look for a brand that has been lab tested.

name: celery
answer: Not at a standard serve. Monash's 2025 retest rated a 75 g serve of celery stalk moderate in mannitol (it used to be high). Monash's public pages give no low amount, and dietitian sites disagree on one.

servings.note: Rated moderate at 1 serve (75 g). No low amount is published outside Monash's app.

changes.text: Monash retested celery stalk: at a standard serve it moved from high to moderate in mannitol. It remains Monash's suggested food for testing mannitol.

disagreements.text: Before the retest, Karlijn's Kitchen (citing Monash) gave 10 g as low, moderate from 15 g and high from 75 g. Her list updated in Sep 2025 gives celery up to 51 g.

notes.text: Monash names celery as one of the vegetables richest in mannitol.
Celery leaves and celeriac (celery root) are reported to be much lower in FODMAPs than the stalk.

faq.a: No public lab result for celery juice was found. Juicing concentrates a lot of stalk into one glass, so it is likely higher than a few sticks.

faq.q: Can I use celery in soup?
faq.a: Monash's lab work shows FODMAPs are water-soluble and move into cooking water, so the broth carries celery's mannitol too. Keep the amount small.

name: spinach
answer: Yes. Monash rates 1½ cups of baby spinach (75 g) low. Dietitian sites citing Monash report baby spinach turns moderate in fructans from 150 g, while mature (English) spinach stays low in much larger amounts.

servings.note: Low amount from Monash; the moderate amount is as reported by Karlijn's Kitchen from Monash's data.
The sources name no FODMAP that rises with the amount; fructans is shown only as a placeholder.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen's 2025 list says mature spinach is low up to 500 g, while Monash's public shopping list only gives the standard 75 g serve.

notes.text: Monash lists a 75 g serve of baby spinach as adding about 3 g of fibre.

faq.q: Is spinach in a smoothie low FODMAP?
faq.a: Yes, at around 1½ cups of baby spinach. The other ingredients, like fruit and milk, usually decide whether the smoothie is low.

faq.q: Is saag or palak low FODMAP?
faq.a: The spinach is fine, but most recipes start with onion and garlic. A version with garlic-infused oil and asafoetida keeps it lower.

name: beetroot
answer: Yes, at a standard serve, after a 2025 retest. Monash now rates 75 g of fresh beetroot low, with GOS and fructans in larger serves. Pickled beetroot is also on Monash's low list at 75 g.

servings.note: Low at 1 serve (75 g); contains GOS and fructans in larger serves.
Monash's shopping list names no FODMAP group here; the groups shown are the ones Monash found in fresh beetroot.

changes.text: Monash retested fresh beetroot: it moved from high (GOS and fructans) to low at a standard serve, and is no longer a fructan test food.

notes.text: In Monash's lab work, pickling cut the FODMAP content of beetroot by 89–97%.
FODMAP Friendly's public list agrees, placing beetroot among its low FODMAP vegetables.

faq.a: No public lab result for beetroot juice was found. A glass may hold more beetroot than the tested 75 g.
Monash lists pickled beetroot at 75 g. We found no public result for plain canned beetroot; check the label for onion.

name: asparagus
answer: No, not at a standard serve. Monash's 2025 retest still rates 75 g of asparagus high, now in fructose. Any low amount is small: dietitian sites citing Monash give from about ⅔ of a spear up to 42 g.

servings.note: Rated high at 1 serve (75 g). No low amount is published by Monash outside its app.

changes.text: Monash retested asparagus: still high at a standard serve, but now for fructose only (it used to be fructose and fructans).

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen (Apr 2024, citing Monash) reports ⅔ of a spear as low, 1 spear as moderate in fructose and 5 spears high. Her list updated in Sep 2025 gives up to 42 g.

notes.text: White asparagus has not been tested by Monash, according to Karlijn's Kitchen.
On FODMAP Friendly's public list, asparagus sits with the high FODMAP vegetables as well.

faq.a: It carries excess fructose: more fructose than glucose. Monash still uses asparagus as its fructose test food.

faq.q: Is a single asparagus spear low FODMAP?
faq.a: Reports say one spear is already moderate in fructose, so keep it to a garnish if fructose bothers you.

name: cauliflower
answer: Yes, at a standard serve, since a 2025 retest. Monash now rates 75 g of white cauliflower low, with fructans in larger serves. It used to be listed high in mannitol, so many older lists are out of date.

servings.note: Rated low at Monash's standard 75 g serve; fructans build up in bigger portions.

changes.text: Monash retested white cauliflower: it moved from high in mannitol to low at a standard serve, with fructans in larger serves.
Monash says cauliflower was retested again and now has a larger low serve. It doesn't give the new amount publicly.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly's public list still puts cauliflower with the high FODMAP vegetables.
A Little Bit Yummy reports both white and purple cauliflower as low at ¾ cup, without giving grams.

notes.text: Monash adds a caution: cauliflower has other gas-forming components besides FODMAPs, so a low rating doesn't rule out bloating.

faq.a: Yes, if the portion stays near 75 g of cauliflower. Pair it with plain rice for a bigger bowl.

faq.q: Is cauliflower still a mannitol food?
faq.a: Not by Monash's 2025 data, which found fructans rather than mannitol. It is no longer suggested for testing mannitol.

name: cucumber
answer: Yes. Monash rates 75 g of cucumber low. After its 2024 fructose review, Monash lists cucumber as moderate from 132 g and high from 178 g, so one cucumber in a big salad is worth weighing.

changes.text: Monash lowered its fructose cut-off for vegetables. Cucumber's moderate amount fell from 360 g to 132 g, and its high amount from 545 g to 178 g. The 75 g low serve did not change.

notes.text: Monash found small cucumbers and pickled gherkins both low at a standard serve.
Cucumber is on FODMAP Friendly's low list as well.

faq.a: Monash rates pickled gherkins low at a standard serve. Check the brine for garlic or onion.
Cucumber is fine, but tzatziki usually has garlic and regular yogurt. Use lactose-free yogurt and garlic-infused oil.

name: kale
answer: Yes. Monash rates ½ cup of chopped kale (75 g) low. Dietitian sites citing Monash report kale turns moderate in GOS only from about 222 g, so a generous handful fits easily.

servings.note: Low amount from Monash; the moderate amount is as reported by Karlijn's Kitchen from Monash's data.

notes.text: Monash lists kale among high-fibre low FODMAP foods, with about 2 g of fibre per 75 g serve.

faq.a: The kale is fine. Check flavoured store-bought chips for garlic or onion powder.

faq.q: Is kale better raw or cooked on a low FODMAP diet?
faq.a: Both count the same by weight. Cooked kale shrinks, so weigh it raw.

name: Brussels sprouts
answer: Yes, at a standard serve, following Monash's 2025 retest. It now rates 75 g of Brussels sprouts low, with fructans only in larger serves. In 2020 Monash had used 75 g of sprouts as an example of a high-fructan serve.

servings.note: Green at a standard 75 g serve in Monash's 2025 testing; larger serves carry more fructans.

changes.text: Monash retested Brussels sprouts: they moved from high in fructans to low at a standard serve, and are no longer a fructan test food.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen's 2024 cabbage guide, written before the retest, gives only 50 g (2 to 3 sprouts) as low; her 2025 list shows 75 g.

notes.text: Sprouts may still be gassy for some people: Monash points to non-FODMAP components in them.

faq.q: How many Brussels sprouts are low FODMAP?
faq.a: Monash gives the low amount by weight, 75 g. Sprouts vary in size, so weigh them rather than counting.

faq.q: Why do Brussels sprouts still make me gassy?
faq.a: Monash says sprouts contain other gas-forming parts besides FODMAPs, so some people react even at a low serve.

name: butternut squash
answer: Only in small amounts. Dietitian sites citing Monash report about ⅓ cup (63 g) of butternut squash as low, moderate from 75 g and high from 85 g, from fructose and fructans. Kabocha (Japanese) pumpkin is the easier swap.

servings.note: Grams as reported by dietitian sites from Monash's data.

disagreements.text: George Eats says Monash has no listing for unpeeled butternut squash, yet gives the 63 g figure for unpeeled butternut on the same page; it is unclear whether the test was raw, cooked, peeled or unpeeled.

notes.text: Monash lists kabocha (Japanese) pumpkin as a low FODMAP vegetable at a standard serve.

faq.q: Is butternut squash soup low FODMAP?
faq.a: Only if the squash per bowl stays small and the soup skips onion and garlic. Bulk it with carrot and potato.

faq.q: Which pumpkin is lowest in FODMAPs?
faq.a: Kabocha (Japanese) pumpkin is on Monash's low list at a standard serve, so it handles bigger portions than butternut.

name: eggplant
answer: Yes. Monash rates 1 cup of eggplant (75 g) low. Larger amounts turn moderate and then high in the polyol sorbitol; dietitian sites citing Monash put the moderate step at about 178 g.

servings.note: Low amount from Monash; the moderate amount is as reported by Karlijn's Kitchen from Monash's data.

notes.text: Monash uses eggplant as an example of a green food with an upper limit: bigger servings become amber, then red, for sorbitol.
Monash lists eggplant as low at a standard serve and suggests it as a plant-based "steak".

faq.a: The eggplant is fine at about 1 cup, but baba ganoush usually has garlic. Make it with garlic-infused oil.
Yes, a lot. Weigh it raw so the portion matches the tested 75 g.

name: lettuce
answer: Yes. Monash lists 75 g of lettuce as a low serve. Butter lettuce is a little tighter: since Monash's 2024 fructose review its low serve is 65 g.

servings.note: No upper limit is published; fructose is the FODMAP Monash names for butter lettuce.

changes.text: Monash lowered its fructose cut-off for vegetables, and butter lettuce's low serve fell from 75 g to 65 g.

notes.text: Monash's Step 1 sheet suggests lettuce as a low FODMAP swap for higher-FODMAP vegetables.
FODMAP Friendly's lab, testing separately, also puts lettuce on its low list.

faq.q: Is a side salad low FODMAP?
faq.a: The leaves usually are. Dressings and toppings decide it: watch for onion, garlic and honey.
Monash's shopping list includes lettuce at 75 g; romaine (cos) is a common type of lettuce.

name: red cabbage
answer: Yes, at a standard serve. Monash rates ½ cup of red cabbage (75 g) low. Above 150 g it turns moderate in fructans, and above 180 g high, so a big slaw can add up.

notes.text: Fermented red cabbage tested moderate at a standard serve in Monash's lab, while raw red cabbage was low.
Karlijn's Kitchen, citing Monash's app, reports the same 75 g low and 150 g moderate amounts.

faq.q: Is red cabbage slaw low FODMAP?
faq.a: Keep the red cabbage near ½ cup per person and use a dressing without onion or garlic.

faq.q: Is red cabbage lower in FODMAPs than white cabbage?
faq.a: Both are low at 75 g. They differ in the FODMAP that rises: fructans in red cabbage, sorbitol in white.

name: pumpkin
answer: Yes, at a normal serve. Monash lists 75 g of kabocha (Japanese or Kent) pumpkin as low. Reported lab data puts it at moderate from 162 g and high from 206 g, from fructans. Canned pumpkin is low at 75 g (⅓ cup). Other squashes, such as butternut, have smaller low serves.

servings.note: The 75 g serve is on Monash's public shopping list. The moderate and high amounts are as reported by dietitian sites from Monash data.
Grams as reported by dietitian sites from Monash data. The pumpkin variety inside the can isn't stated.

changes.text: Kabocha first tested with no FODMAPs at all. A later Monash retest found fructans in bigger portions, so it now has a 75 g low serve.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly's lab reportedly rates Japanese or Kent pumpkin lower: 57 g raw, or 75 g cooked with a 94 g maximum.
For canned pumpkin, FODMAP Friendly reportedly allows 120 g, up to 150 g, and found GOS as well as fructans.

notes.text: Monash lists Japanese pumpkin among its low FODMAP swaps in its Step 1 guide.
In Monash's roasted pepper and pumpkin dip, using butternut instead of Japanese pumpkin means splitting the batch into more servings to stay within limits.

faq.q: Is butternut squash low FODMAP like pumpkin?
faq.a: Only in a smaller portion. Dietitian sites report Monash's low serve for unpeeled butternut at 63 g, below kabocha's 75 g.
The filling can fit if each slice holds no more than about 75 g of canned pumpkin. The crust, milk and sweetener need checking too.

name: arugula
answer: Yes. Monash's standard serve of arugula (rocket) is 1 cup, about 35 g, and it reportedly found only trace FODMAPs. Dietitian sites say it stayed low up to 500 g, the largest amount tested, so it works as a salad base.

servings.note: Only trace FODMAPs were found, so this is a normal portion, not a limit. The source names no FODMAP group.

changes.text: For years Monash reported no FODMAPs in arugula. An app update changed this to trace amounts, still with no upper limit.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen gives the largest still-low amount instead of a standard serve: up to 500 g.

faq.a: The arugula is fine. Most pesto recipes add garlic, so use garlic-infused oil in its place.

name: bok choy
answer: Yes, at a standard serve. Monash lists 75 g of bok choy, about 1 cup chopped, as low. Dietitian sites report a moderate amount of sorbitol from 100 g, so a very large stir-fry portion can tip it over.

servings.note: The moderate amount is as reported by Karlijn's Kitchen from Monash data.

notes.text: Monash's Step 1 guide and its public food list both name bok choy as a low FODMAP vegetable.

faq.q: Can I have bok choy in a stir-fry every day?
faq.a: Yes, if each meal stays near 75 g. Bigger amounts add sorbitol, which adds up with other polyol foods in the same meal.

name: leek
answer: Partly. The dark green leaves are low: Monash's serve is 1 cup chopped (75 g), and they reportedly stayed low up to 500 g. The white bulb holds fructans, so only about 14 g of it (2 generous tablespoons, finely chopped) is reported as low.

servings.note: Reported to stay low up to 500 g, the most Monash tested.
No moderate or high amount has been published for the bulb.

changes.text: Monash's leaf serve was first listed as 100 g, then 75 g. A small low serve for the white bulb (14 g) was added later, and an unclear mixed leaf-and-bulb entry was removed.

disagreements.text: Monash's public diet sheets still list leek among high-FODMAP vegetables without saying which part, which fits the bulb rather than the leaves.
FODMAP Friendly's lab reportedly rates ½ cup (37 g) of leaves as low with an 82 g maximum, and 47 g of bulb as low.

notes.text: Monash now uses raw leek bulb as one of its fructan test foods in the reintroduction phase.
Older lab data measured about 0.5 g of fructans per 100 g of whole leek, far less than onion at about 1.8 g.

faq.q: Is leek and potato soup low FODMAP?
faq.a: Only when it's made with the green leaves. Fructans from the white bulb dissolve into the soup, so a classic version is likely high.

name: onion
answer: No. Monash lists onion as high in fructans. Only tiny amounts test low: about 10 g of red onion is the reported Monash low serve, and FODMAP Friendly reportedly rates brown onion high from 30 g. Drained large pickled onions are a lower-FODMAP option.

servings.note: Monash has published no low serve for these onions. The 30 g high point is FODMAP Friendly's, as reported by a dietitian site.
Reported Monash low serve. No moderate or high amount has been published.
Reported to be high in fructans above 107 g. Small pickled onions tested very differently.

changes.text: Monash's low serve for large pickled onions was first 45 g and was later raised to 60 g.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly's lab reportedly allows 26 g of brown onion and 27 g of red onion, more than Monash's 10 g of red onion.
George Eats reports large pickled onions as low up to 84 g, with moderate fructans from 85 g.

notes.text: Older lab data measured about 1.8 g of fructans per 100 g of white onion.
Monash keeps onion of any variety as its test food for onion fructans in the reintroduction phase.
Fructans dissolve in water but not in oil, so onion-infused oil keeps the flavor without the fructans.

faq.q: Does cooking onion make it low FODMAP?
faq.a: Not in normal cooking: fructans move into the water of soups and sauces. Monash found microwaving diced onion in water cut its FODMAPs by 71%, but it still wasn't low.
Yes, as long as the onion pieces are taken out. The fructans stay in the onion, not the oil.

name: spring onion
answer: The green tops, yes. Monash reports ¾ cup (75 g) of spring onion greens as low, with a moderate amount of fructose from 97 g. The white bulb carries fructans: a 32 g Monash low serve is reported, but many guides still say to skip the bulb at first.

servings.note: Grams as reported by dietitian sites from Monash's latest retest.
Reported Monash low serve. No moderate or high amount has been published.

changes.text: Early tests found no FODMAPs in 16 g of greens. A September 2022 retest set 75 g as low and moderate from 265 g. A later retest kept 75 g but moved the moderate point down to 97 g.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly lists the spring onion bulb as high. Its lab reportedly rates scallion greens low at 16 g, with a 160 g maximum.
One George Eats recipe says Monash regards the greens as having negligible FODMAPs, which doesn't match the 97 g moderate point above.

notes.text: Monash suggests the green tops as a garnish for onion flavor without the fructans.
Older lab data found the spring onion bulb rich in fructans, at about 6.3 g per 100 g.

faq.q: Are scallions and spring onions the same thing?
faq.a: Monash lists them as one food. In the US, spring onions can be a variety with a larger bulb, so sticking to the green parts is the simplest rule.

name: shallots
answer: No. Shallots are among the richest sources of fructans, at about 8.9 g per 100 g in lab tests, roughly five times as much as onion. Monash reportedly tested large amounts and found no low serve. Spring onion greens, chives or garlic-infused oil give a similar savory note.

servings.note: No low serve has been published by Monash, and no gram amount for the high point is public.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly's lab reportedly rates 1 g of shallot as low, an amount too small to matter in most cooking.

notes.text: Lab data put shallots at about 8.9 g of fructans per 100 g, behind only garlic and Jerusalem artichoke among the vegetables measured.
Monash names shallots among the main high-FODMAP ingredients in East and South East Asian cooking, including fried shallots and curry pastes.

faq.a: No test of fried shallots has been published. Fructans don't move into the frying oil, so they stay in the crispy shallot.

name: fennel
answer: Yes, at a normal serve. Monash's retested low serve is ¾ cup (75 g) of raw fennel bulb. Reported lab data shows a moderate amount of fructose from 145 g and high from 195 g, when fructans appear too. The feathery fronds are low at 3 tablespoons (15 g).

servings.note: Grams as reported by dietitian sites from Monash's retest.

changes.text: Monash's first low serve for raw fennel bulb was ½ cup (49 g). A retest raised it to ¾ cup (75 g).

disagreements.text: George Eats gives the largest still-low amount instead: up to 144 g of bulb, as of August 2026.
FODMAP Friendly reportedly rates ½ cup (48 g) of bulb as low with a 144 g maximum, and names fructans and mannitol.

notes.text: Fennel seeds were reported low at 1 teaspoon (2 g) by both Monash and FODMAP Friendly.

faq.a: The tests used raw bulb, so weigh it before cooking and keep to about 75 g per person.

name: bell pepper
answer: Green bell pepper, yes: Monash lists 75 g as low, with fructans only moderate from 250 g. Red is a different story: about 43 g (⅓ cup) is low, with fructose moderate from 57 g and high from 75 g. Yellow and orange peppers sit close to red.

servings.note: The 75 g serve is on Monash's public shopping list. The moderate and high amounts are as reported by dietitian sites.
Grams as reported by dietitian sites from Monash's retest.

changes.text: Monash first found no FODMAPs in red bell pepper, and its January 2021 fibre guide still listed 75 g as a low serve. A retest cut the low serve to 43 g.
Green bell pepper's low serve went from 52 g in early testing to 75 g after a retest.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly's lab reportedly rates 75 g of red pepper as low, with a maximum of 750 g, later 825 g. For yellow pepper it later found no low amount.
Karlijn's Kitchen gives yellow and orange together as 38 g low, 51 g moderate and 75 g high.

notes.text: Monash's diet sheets list red bell pepper among high-FODMAP vegetables and green bell pepper as the low swap.

faq.q: Are roasted red peppers low FODMAP?
faq.a: We haven't found a public test of roasted peppers. Keep to about 43 g of red pepper per serve, or mix in green pepper for volume.

name: zucchini
answer: Yes, in a modest serve. Monash's current diet sheet lists 65 g of zucchini as low. Reported lab data shows moderate fructans from 75 g and high from 87 g, so one medium zucchini, about 195 g, is more than a single low serve.

servings.note: The 65 g serve is from Monash's 2026 diet sheet. The moderate and high amounts are as reported by dietitian sites.

disagreements.text: George Eats reports zucchini as low up to 74 g as of August 2026, with moderate fructans from 75 g. An earlier report put the low serve at 67 g.
FODMAP Friendly's lab reportedly rates 75 g of raw green zucchini as low, with a 525 g maximum.

notes.text: Monash weighs one medium zucchini at about 195 g in its recipes.

faq.a: It depends more on the flour and sweetener. Spread across a whole loaf, the zucchini in one slice is usually a small amount.

name: edamame
answer: Yes, at a normal serve. Dietitian sites report a Monash low serve of 75 g of shelled edamame, and the newest report says it stays low up to about 195 g before fructans turn moderate. Edamame behaves very differently from mature soybeans, which are high FODMAP.

servings.note: Grams as reported by dietitian sites from Monash data. See below for the larger still-low amount.

changes.text: Earlier reports gave ½ cup (90 g, cooked) as the low serve, with high fructans from 210 g.

disagreements.text: George Eats reports edamame as low up to 195 g as of August 2026, with moderate fructans in larger serves.

notes.text: Mature soybeans are high in GOS and fructans, so whole soybeans and milk made from them are not the same as edamame.

faq.q: Does edamame have GOS like other beans?
faq.a: Reported testing names fructans, not GOS, as the FODMAP that builds up in large edamame servings.

name: jalapeño
answer: Yes, in normal amounts. Dietitian sites report a Monash low serve of 30 g of raw jalapeño (one small chile), with fructose moderate from about 40 g. Pickled jalapeños had only trace FODMAPs and stayed low up to 500 g, the most tested.

servings.note: Grams as reported by dietitian sites from Monash data.
Only trace FODMAPs were found, and it stayed low up to 500 g, so this is a normal portion, not a limit.

disagreements.text: George Eats gives the largest still-low amount for raw jalapeño instead: up to 39 g.

notes.text: Peppers contain capsaicin, which can cause heartburn or stomach pain in some people for reasons unrelated to FODMAPs.

faq.q: Is salsa with jalapeño low FODMAP?
faq.a: The jalapeño is fine in small amounts, but most store-bought salsa also has onion and garlic, so read the label.

name: sauerkraut
answer: Only a small spoonful. Fermenting cabbage turns some of its sugar into mannitol, a polyol. Monash rates 1 tablespoon as low and a full cup as high. Dietitian sites report 2 tablespoons (23 g) as low, with a moderate amount of mannitol from 35 g.

servings.note: Grams as reported by Karlijn's Kitchen. Monash says a full cup is high but gives no gram figure for it.

changes.text: Monash now uses white-cabbage sauerkraut as one of its mannitol test foods in the reintroduction phase.

disagreements.text: Monash's 2016 post put the low serve at 1 tablespoon, smaller than the 2 tablespoons (23 g) that dietitian sites now report.

notes.text: Plain cabbage is low in a 1 cup serve, but the same cup fermented into sauerkraut is high in mannitol.
Red cabbage sauerkraut rated moderate in Monash's table, against high for the white version. A dietitian site reported it low at ½ cup in older app data.

faq.q: Can I eat sauerkraut for gut health on a low FODMAP diet?
faq.a: A spoonful fits. Larger servings add mannitol, so try them during the reintroduction phase instead.

name: kimchi
answer: In a small side portion. Dietitian sites report that Monash lists 47 g of kimchi as low, with a moderate amount of mannitol from 71 g. As with sauerkraut, fermentation creates mannitol. Recipes and brands vary, so the tested kimchi may not match yours.

servings.note: Grams as reported by Karlijn's Kitchen from the Monash app.

changes.text: In 2016 a dietitian site noted Monash hadn't tested kimchi yet. By 2024 a tested serve of 47 g was being reported.

notes.text: Lactic fermentation converts fructose in cabbage into mannitol, which is why fermented cabbage tests higher than fresh.

faq.a: Not in a side-dish portion of about 47 g. A big bowl adds mannitol, so keep it as a topping or side.

name: ginger
answer: Yes. Monash's low serve for fresh ginger is 5 g, raised from 3 g, with no upper limit given, and FODMAP Friendly reportedly found no FODMAPs at all. Fresh ginger is a handy way to add flavor in place of onion and garlic.

servings.note: No upper limit was given. The source names no FODMAP group.

changes.text: Monash's serve for fresh ginger was first 1 teaspoon (3 g) and was raised to 5 g after more testing.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly reportedly found no FODMAPs in fresh ginger or in plain pickled ginger.

notes.text: Monash names ginger, with garlic-infused oil and spring onion greens, as a versatile flavor base for low FODMAP cooking.
Ginger ale is reported low up to 244 g in Monash data. No Monash entry for ground ginger was found.

faq.a: Ginger tea itself hasn't been tested, but a homemade infusion of fresh ginger is likely fine given ginger's results.
No public test was found. It's likely similar to fresh ginger, but that's an assumption, not a lab result.

name: cinnamon
answer: Probably fine in normal amounts. Monash names cinnamon among spices used in low FODMAP cooking, and a dietitian site reports a Monash-tested serve of 1 teaspoon. We found no public gram figure, so we can't show a lab-tested amount here.

estimateAnswer.line: A 1 teaspoon serve is reported to have passed Monash testing, but no gram figure is public.

servings.note: No public gram figure, so no amounts are shown. The source names no FODMAP group.

notes.text: Monash lists cinnamon in its Mexican cuisine row and other cuisine rows of low FODMAP herbs and spices.
Monash advises avoiding seasoning mixes and blends, which can hide garlic or onion.

faq.q: Can I bake with cinnamon on a low FODMAP diet?
faq.a: Yes. A teaspoon spread through a recipe is a small amount per serve; the flour and sweetener matter far more.

name: cilantro
answer: Yes. Fresh cilantro (coriander leaves) is reported low at 1 cup in Monash testing, which weighs only about 16 g. Monash also lists fresh herbs among its low FODMAP staples. Dried coriander seed is a separate spice, reported low up to 20 g.

servings.note: No moderate or high amount has been published. The source names no FODMAP group.

notes.text: Dried coriander is reported low up to 20 g in Monash data, with moderate fructose in larger serves.
Monash lists coriander with parsley, thyme, basil and rosemary as fresh herbs that add flavor without FODMAPs.

faq.q: Is cilantro lime rice low FODMAP?
faq.a: The cilantro and rice are fine. Check any added garlic or onion, which many recipes include.

name: basil
answer: Yes. Monash testing reportedly rates 1 cup of fresh basil, about 16 g, as low, and Monash lists fresh and dried herbs among low FODMAP staples. Basil is so light that a cup is a generous handful. Classic pesto is the catch, because of its garlic.

servings.note: No moderate or high amount has been published. The source names no FODMAP group.

notes.text: Monash lists basil in Italian and Indian cooking and Thai basil in Asian cooking as low FODMAP flavorings.

faq.a: Basil is fine, but most pesto has garlic. Make it with garlic-infused oil, and check the nut amount per serve.

name: paprika
answer: Yes, in normal amounts. Monash's reported low serve for paprika is 1 teaspoon (2 g), and larger amounts add fructose. Newer reports say smoked paprika reaches a moderate amount at 5 g. FODMAP Friendly reportedly found no FODMAPs in paprika.

servings.note: Reported Monash low serve. No upper limit was given at the time.

changes.text: George Eats reported that Monash added an upper threshold for regular paprika, with moderate fructose after 7 g.

disagreements.text: Reports on smoked paprika differ: one George Eats page says it is low up to 5 g, another says it is moderate at 5 g.
FODMAP Friendly reportedly lists paprika as free of FODMAPs.

notes.text: Monash lists paprika in Mexican, Moroccan and Spanish cooking as a low FODMAP spice.

faq.a: In small amounts. Reports put its moderate point at about 5 g, so keep the amount per serve modest.

name: cumin
answer: Yes, in normal amounts. A dietitian site reports that Monash tested ground cumin and black cumin seed and rated 2 g portions as low. Monash also lists cumin among spices for low FODMAP cooking. Spice blends are the risk, since many add garlic or onion.

servings.note: Reported Monash low serve. No upper limit has been published. The source names no FODMAP group.

notes.text: Monash names cumin in its Mexican, Indian, Middle Eastern and Moroccan rows of low FODMAP spices.
Monash's shopping list allows most spices, as long as they don't contain garlic or onion.

faq.q: Is whole cumin seed low FODMAP?
faq.a: Black cumin seed (kalonji) was also reported low at 2 g. Regular whole cumin seed is likely similar, but we found no separate public test.

name: garlic powder
answer: Usually not. Garlic powder is dried garlic, and Monash lists it beside fresh garlic as a high-fructan ingredient to look for on labels. Drying removes water, so the fructans are more concentrated by weight. No lab-tested serve is public. Garlic-infused oil is the usual swap.

estimateAnswer.line: Monash lists garlic powder as a high-fructan ingredient. No public lab amount exists.

servings.note: Not lab-tested in public data. Estimated from what it's made of.

notes.text: Fresh garlic is high in fructans even at 3 g, and dried garlic has had its water taken out.
Monash's label guide also flags garlic salt and garlic extract as fructan sources.

faq.q: How much garlic powder is too much?
faq.a: No public lab amount exists. Since fresh garlic is already high at 3 g, assume garlic powder is high in any normal amount.

name: onion powder
answer: Usually not. Onion powder is dried onion, and Monash lists it with onion as a high-fructan ingredient to check for on labels. Drying concentrates the fructans by weight, and no lab-tested serve is public. Spring onion greens, chives or onion-infused oil give onion flavor instead.

estimateAnswer.line: Monash lists onion powder as a high-fructan ingredient. No public lab amount exists.

servings.note: Not lab-tested in public data. Estimated from what it's made of.

notes.text: Many packaged flavors use onion and garlic powder, so it turns up in snacks, stocks and seasonings.
Monash suggests a pinch of asafoetida powder for onion flavor in curries, rice dishes and stews.

faq.a: No. Monash lists onion salt alongside onion powder as a high-fructan ingredient.

name: chives
answer: Yes. Chives are one of the easiest onion swaps: Monash and FODMAP Friendly both reportedly found no FODMAPs, with a standard serve of 4 g. Dried chives (2 g serve) and Asian or garlic chives (80 g serve) are reported low too.

servings.note: No FODMAPs were reportedly detected, so this is a normal portion, not a limit. The source names no FODMAP group.

disagreements.text: George Eats gives the largest still-low amount instead: up to 500 g per person.

notes.text: Monash's FAQ names chives, with spring onion greens and asafoetida, as ways to add flavor without onion or garlic.

faq.a: Yes. Asian (garlic) chives were reported low at an 80 g serve, and they add a mild garlic taste.

name: banana
answer: Yes, if it's firm. A firm banana is low up to about 95 g and turns moderate in fructans from 100 g. Ripe bananas carry more fructans: about a third of one (37 g) is the low amount, and 47 g is moderate.

changes.text: Monash retested bananas: ripe ones moved to high in fructans, firm ones stayed low. Monash links the change to cold storage and ripening, which raise fructans.
Monash's 2021 fibre article listed one medium firm banana (100 g) as low. Newer dietitian listings give 95 g as low and 100 g as moderate, so we show the newer numbers.

disagreements.text: George Eats gives the most that stays low as 99 g for a firm banana and 46 g for a ripe one. Karlijn's Kitchen (2023) gave 35 g for ripe.

notes.text: If ripe bananas don't bother you, Monash says there's no need to cut them out.
FODMAP Friendly also rates unripe banana as low and says FODMAPs rise as the skin turns yellow and brown.

faq.a: It depends on how much banana each slice holds and the flour. Recipes usually use ripe bananas, which have the smaller low amount, so check the banana per slice.

faq.q: Are green bananas better than yellow ones?
faq.a: For FODMAPs, yes. Firm bananas have a much bigger low serve than ripe, spotty ones.

name: grapes
answer: Only a few. Monash cut the low serve in 2024 to 2 grapes: about 11 g of green grapes or 10 g of red. From about 15 grapes (75 g) they are high in excess fructose. Green grapes turn moderate at 15 g.

changes.text: Grapes used to be low in a 1 cup serve. Monash's 2021 retest set 6 grapes as low (32 g green, 28 g red) and 15 grapes (75 g) as high.
Monash retested again and lowered the low serve to 2 grapes; dietitian sites report that 3 or more already contain excess fructose.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly's results, as reported by a dietitian site, are far more generous: 150 g of red seedless and 24 g of white seedless grapes.
Karlijn's Kitchen's 2023 list still shows 30 g (6 grapes), which predates the 2024 retest.

notes.text: Monash thinks sweeter modern grape varieties may explain the extra fructose found in retests.

faq.q: Why do some lists still say a cup of grapes is fine?
faq.a: They were printed before Monash's 2021 and 2024 retests. Newer Monash data allows only a couple of grapes.

faq.q: Are raisins the same as grapes for FODMAPs?
faq.a: No. Drying concentrates the sugars, so raisins have their own, even smaller low amount.

name: pineapple
answer: Yes. One cup of chopped fresh pineapple (140 g) is low in Monash's published fibre guide. Fructans rise with bigger bowls, and a George Eats listing puts moderate at 195 g.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen (2024) puts moderate at 200 g instead of 195 g. George Eats gives 194 g as the most that stays low.

notes.text: Canned and dried pineapple have smaller low amounts than fresh. Karlijn's Kitchen lists about 97 g for canned in juice and 67 g in syrup, and says 25 g of dried is already moderate.
Monash and FODMAP Friendly both list pineapple among their low FODMAP fruits.

faq.a: In a smaller serve than fresh. Pineapple canned in syrup has the smallest low amount, so drain it and keep the portion modest.

name: blueberries
answer: Yes, generously. After a 2022 retest Monash moved blueberries to low in a 1 cup serve, and dietitian sites report they stay low up to 500 g in its data. Monash and FODMAP Friendly both list them as low.

servings.note: 500 g is the largest amount reported as still low, not a standard serve. No source names a limiting FODMAP at the amounts tested; the group shown is a placeholder.

changes.text: Blueberries used to be limited to about 20 berries. A 2022 Monash retest moved them to low in 1 cup serves.

notes.text: Monash suggests frozen berries as an easy way to keep low FODMAP fruit in the diet out of season, for example a handful on porridge.
Monash and FODMAP Friendly both list blueberries among their low FODMAP fruits.

faq.a: The blueberries aren't the problem. Most muffins use wheat flour and sometimes honey, so look for a recipe made with gluten-free flour.

faq.q: Why did older lists say to limit blueberries?
faq.a: Those lists predate Monash's 2022 retest, which found a much larger low serve.

name: dates
answer: In small amounts. About 5 dried pitted dates (30 g) are low, rising to moderate in sorbitol and fructans from 46 g. A single Medjool date (20 g) is low; two are moderate and three are high.

disagreements.text: George Eats gives the most that stays low as 45 g for common pitted dates and 39 g for Medjool.

notes.text: Drying concentrates the sugars, and Monash has found fructans in dried fruit that the fresh fruit doesn't have.
Both Monash and FODMAP Friendly put dried fruit in their high column, which is why dates come with a small serve.

faq.a: We haven't found published lab data for fresh dates, only for dried and Medjool.

faq.q: Can I use dates in baking?
faq.a: Yes, if each serving keeps to the low amount. Divide the dates in the recipe by the number of portions.

name: apple
answer: Not in a normal serve. Apples are high in excess fructose and sorbitol. Only a small piece is low: about 20 g of unpeeled Pink Lady. It turns moderate from 31 g, and one medium apple (200 g) is high.

disagreements.text: Granny Smith figures differ: Karlijn's Kitchen (2023) lists 25 g as low, while George Eats (2026) says unpeeled Granny Smith stays low up to 42 g.

notes.text: Monash names apples among the fruits richest in both excess fructose and sorbitol, and lists apple juice as high.
George Eats reports applesauce is low only in tiny amounts and reconstituted apple juice is high at half a glass.

faq.q: Is apple cider vinegar low FODMAP?
faq.a: Vinegar is a different food from the fruit. See our apple cider vinegar page for its tested amount.
Only a little. Peeled apples still have a very small low serve and are high at one medium fruit.

name: raspberries
answer: Yes, in a small bowl. Monash lists about 30 raspberries (60 g) as a low serve. From 75 g they turn moderate in excess fructose, so keep to about a third of a cup per sitting.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen and Diet vs Disease list 58 g. George Eats gives 74 g as the most that stays low.

notes.text: A Little Bit Yummy says Monash's 2026 data still puts the serve at about ⅓ cup (60 g), and suggests a scale since berry size varies.
Raspberries are a good fibre source within their low serve, according to Monash.

faq.q: Can I eat raspberries and strawberries together?
faq.a: Both are limited by excess fructose, so a full serve of each adds up. Half a serve of each is the cautious way.

name: cherries
answer: Mostly no. Cherries are high in sorbitol and excess fructose at a normal serve. A dietitian listing based on Monash data gives only 20 g of pitted fresh cherries as low.

servings.note: No public source gives the moderate or high amount. Monash and FODMAP Friendly both list cherries as high.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly says fresh cherries are not low FODMAP and gives no smaller allowed amount.

notes.text: Monash names cherries among the fruits high in both excess fructose and sorbitol.
Karlijn's Kitchen puts cherries on its avoid list for the elimination phase, as the low amount is 20 g or less.

faq.q: Are dried or canned cherries any better?
faq.a: We haven't found public lab data for them. Dried fruit usually concentrates FODMAPs, so don't assume it's lower.

name: orange
answer: Yes. One medium peeled orange (130 g) is a low serve in Monash's published fibre guide. A George Eats listing puts moderate, from excess fructose, at 152 g.

disagreements.text: George Eats gives 151 g as the most that stays low and notes the Monash app now lists only navel oranges.

notes.text: Freshly squeezed orange juice has a much smaller low amount than the whole fruit: about 72 g in one dietitian listing.
Monash and FODMAP Friendly both list oranges among low FODMAP fruits.

faq.a: Only a small glass. Juicing packs several oranges into one drink, so the whole fruit is the easier choice.

name: cantaloupe
answer: Yes. Monash's 2026 info sheet lists ¾ cup of cantaloupe (120 g) as low. Fructans rise with bigger slices, reaching moderate at about 150 g.

disagreements.text: Diet vs Disease lists 121 g, and George Eats gives 149 g as the most that stays low.

notes.text: A Little Bit Yummy suggests cantaloupe as a swap for grapes on a cheese board since grapes were retested.

faq.q: Is cantaloupe lower in FODMAPs than watermelon?
faq.a: Yes, by a lot. Cantaloupe has a ¾ cup low serve, while watermelon is low only in a spoonful.

name: mango
answer: No, except a bite. Mango is high in excess fructose. Newer dietitian listings based on Monash data give about 7 g as low and moderate from 9 g, far less than the 40 g quoted on older lists.

changes.text: Older listings gave 40 g as low, 50 g as moderate and 140 g as high. Listings from late 2024 onward give about 7 g, so mango appears to have been retested.

notes.text: Monash names mango among the fruits particularly high in excess fructose. FODMAP Friendly also lists it as high.

faq.a: We haven't found a public low amount for dried mango. Dried fruit concentrates sugars, so expect it to be higher than fresh.

name: kiwi fruit
answer: Yes. Two small peeled kiwi fruit (150 g) are a low serve for both green and gold kiwi in Monash's published fibre guide. Larger amounts add fructans.

disagreements.text: George Eats says green kiwi turns moderate in fructans only above 275 g and gold above 178 g. Karlijn's Kitchen (2023) listed 240 g (3 kiwis) of green as low.

notes.text: Green kiwi is one of the higher-fibre low FODMAP fruits in Monash's fibre guide.
FODMAP Friendly also rates 2 kiwi fruit as low and mentions them as a daily option for people prone to constipation.

faq.a: We haven't found lab data for unpeeled kiwi. The tested serves are for peeled fruit.

name: cranberries
answer: Dried cranberries are low in a small handful: about 22 g in a recent dietitian listing based on Monash data. Monash says dried cranberries turn high only in larger serves. Fructans are the main FODMAP.

servings.note: No public source gives the moderate or high amount.

disagreements.text: Low amounts for dried cranberries vary: 22 g (Diet vs Disease), 15 g (Karlijn's Kitchen, 2023) and a preliminary Monash figure of 1 tablespoon (9 g) from 2015.
For fresh cranberries, Karlijn's Kitchen lists 90 g as low and A Little Bit Yummy 50 g. We don't show a bar until the figures agree.

notes.text: Monash suggests dried cranberries as a low FODMAP dried-fruit snack and lists cranberry juice among low FODMAP options.
Monash's 2015 berry analysis found cranberries contain fructans, so big servings are the thing to avoid.

faq.a: Monash publishes a cranberry sauce recipe for 16 servings that uses dried cranberries, blueberries and cranberry juice. Shop sauces vary, so check the label.

name: lemon
answer: Yes, for normal cooking amounts. Monash uses a tablespoon of fresh lemon juice (20 g) as a low serve in its meal example. Dietitian sites report it stays low in far larger amounts.

servings.note: 20 g is Monash's example serve, not an upper limit.

disagreements.text: Diet vs Disease lists 21 mL, close to Monash's tablespoon. Others report far more: 125 g (Karlijn's Kitchen, 2023) and up to 177 g, with moderate fructans from 178 g (George Eats).

notes.text: Monash suggests a little cut lemon in water as a low FODMAP way to flavour drinks.
George Eats reports lemon zest is low in amounts far beyond anything a recipe uses.

faq.a: Yes. A squeeze of lemon in water is well under the tested amounts.

faq.q: Is the whole lemon low FODMAP?
faq.a: Public data covers lemon juice and zest. We haven't found a figure for eating the whole fruit.

name: papaya
answer: Yes. Monash lists papaya among its low FODMAP fruits, and dietitian sites report that both green and yellow papaya stay low up to 500 g in its data. That makes it one of the most generous fruits.

servings.note: 500 g is the largest amount reported as still low, not a standard serve. No source names a limiting FODMAP at the amounts tested; the group shown is a placeholder.

notes.text: Monash lists yellow papaya as a low FODMAP swap and includes papaya in its shopping list and summer fruit picks.

faq.q: Is green papaya salad low FODMAP?
faq.a: The green papaya is. Thai-style dressings often add garlic and shallots, so ask for them to be left out or check the recipe.

name: raisins
answer: Only a pinch. Recent dietitian listings based on Monash data give about 4 g of raisins as low, limited by excess fructose. Sultanas are listed at about 7 g. Older advice said a tablespoon (13 g).

servings.note: No public source gives the moderate or high amount.
No public source gives the moderate or high amount.

changes.text: In 2015 Monash listed 1 tablespoon (13 g) of raisins as low at a half serve. Listings from 2024 and 2025 give 4 g, which suggests a retest.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen still gives 13 g on an older recipe page but 4 g on a page updated in December 2025.

notes.text: Drying concentrates sugars, and Monash has found fructans in dried fruit that the fresh fruit lacks.
Both Monash and FODMAP Friendly put dried fruit in the high column.

faq.q: Are raisins in cereal or baking a problem?
faq.a: They can be, because the low amount is tiny. Divide the raisins in a recipe by the servings to check.

name: honeydew melon
answer: Yes, in a half-cup serve. About ½ cup of honeydew (90 g) is low. Fructans rise from 116 g (moderate), and a full cup (150 g) is high.

disagreements.text: Diet vs Disease lists 92 g. George Eats gives 115 g as the most that stays low.

faq.q: Is honeydew better than watermelon on a low FODMAP diet?
faq.a: Yes. Honeydew has a half-cup low serve, while watermelon is low only in a spoonful.

name: olives
answer: Yes. Plain green and black olives are reported to stay low FODMAP up to 500 g in Monash's data, and FODMAP Friendly lists olives as low. Marinated olives are different: garlic or onion in the mix is the problem.

servings.form: green or black olives, in brine
servings.note: 500 g is the largest amount reported as still low, far more than a normal portion. No source names a limiting FODMAP at the amounts tested; the group shown is a placeholder.

notes.text: Check the label on marinated or stuffed olives: garlic and onion are common, and both are high in fructans.

faq.a: We haven't found a separate lab result for Kalamata. Plain green and black olives tested low.
Yes. See our olive oil page for the details.

name: coconut
answer: Yes, in measured amounts. ⅔ cup of fresh coconut flesh (64 g) is low in Monash's fibre guide, with sorbitol moderate from 96 g. Shredded coconut is low at ½ cup (30 g).

disagreements.text: Diet vs Disease lists 81 g of fresh flesh as low, and George Eats gives 95 g as the most that stays low.
For shredded coconut, Karlijn's Kitchen puts moderate at 45 g, but George Eats says 35 g.

notes.text: Coconut flour is a different story: it's reported high in fructose, sorbitol and fructans at 100 g.
Fresh coconut is one of the higher-fibre foods in Monash's low FODMAP fibre guide.

faq.a: It depends on the type and amount. See our coconut milk page.
In a glass-sized serve, according to dietitian sites. Larger amounts add sorbitol and fructans.

name: watermelon
answer: No. Watermelon is high in excess fructose, and at 150 g also in mannitol and fructans. Only about 18 g, a few teaspoons, is low; it's moderate from 24 g and high from 150 g.

disagreements.text: George Eats gives 23 g as the most that stays low.

notes.text: Monash and FODMAP Friendly both list watermelon in their high FODMAP fruit column.
Monash names watermelon among the fruits particularly high in excess fructose.

faq.q: Can I have watermelon once I finish the elimination phase?
faq.a: If you tolerate fructose, mannitol and fructans in reintroduction, you may handle more. Test it on its own.
We haven't found lab data for it. It comes from the same high-FODMAP fruit, so expect it to be high.

name: sourdough bread
answer: Yes, at about 2 slices. FODMAP sites citing Monash's tests put white wheat sourdough low at 109 g (2 slices) and wholemeal wheat sourdough at 97 g. The long rise lets the starter's yeast and bacteria break down much of the fructan in the flour.

servings.note: Weights come from FODMAP sites that cite Monash. Monash's own posts say tested sourdoughs meet its low criteria but don't print the grams.

changes.text: Kate Scarlata reported that Monash had tested US white and wholemeal wheat sourdoughs and found 2 slices low. Before that, spelt sourdough was the main sourdough with a published low serve.

disagreements.text: Spelt sourdough: Monash's 2015 post lists 2 slices as low but gives no weight, while Karlijn's Kitchen lists 41 g (2.5 slices). Slice size varies a lot between loaves, so weighing helps.

notes.text: Monash explains two reasons sourdough can be low: spelt flour starts with less fructan than modern wheat, and a proving time of often more than 12 hours lets the culture ferment the FODMAPs.
Both Monash's shopping list and FODMAP Friendly's food list put sourdough bread on the low side.
Check the label for honey or high fructose corn syrup, and look for a sourdough starter or culture in the ingredients.

faq.a: Only if it's made with a real starter and a long rise. Look for a sourdough culture on the ingredient list and skip loaves sweetened with honey.

faq.q: Can I eat sourdough toast at every meal?
faq.a: Monash serve sizes are per meal, so a low serve at breakfast and another at dinner is how the diet is set up. Leave a few hours between them.

name: oats
answer: Yes, in a half-cup serve. Monash lists ½ cup of uncooked rolled oats (52 g) as a low FODMAP serve. Quick oats have a smaller reported low serve of 23 g, and larger bowls add GOS and fructans.

changes.text: Monash's 2015 wheat-swap table suggested ¼ cup of oats. Its 2021 fibre guide lists ½ cup (52 g) of rolled oats as the low serve.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen notes that Quaker quick oats are listed low at 40 g while generic quick oats are low only at 23 g. A tested brand can differ from the average.

notes.text: In Monash's lab analysis of 55 grain products, oats were at the low end for fructans, about 0.11 g per portion.
Monash says oats contain gluten but are fairly low in FODMAPs, so they fit a low FODMAP diet in the right serve.
A ½ cup serve of rolled oats adds about 5 g of fibre.

faq.a: Yes, if you keep to about ½ cup of dry rolled oats and cook them with a low FODMAP milk. Honey and dried fruit on top add FODMAPs.
Soaking doesn't change the oat serve, so stay near ½ cup dry. The yogurt, milk and fruit you add count too.

name: rice
answer: Yes. Rice is one of the easiest low FODMAP staples. Monash researchers found no measurable fructan in it, and A Little Bit Yummy, citing Monash, gives 1 cup of cooked white rice (190 g) as the serve. Newer reports put the low amount much higher.

servings.note: A typical serve, not a limit: later reports rate much more as low.

disagreements.text: George Eats (checked August 2026) reports that Monash now rates cooked white, jasmine, basmati and arborio rice low up to 500 g.

notes.text: In Monash's 2011 analysis of grain foods, rice had 0 g of fructan per portion, the lowest of all products tested.
A 2024 lab study of cooked grains found white long-grain, basmati, jasmine and arborio rice all below the 0.3 g fructan cut-off per serve.
Rice snacks are different: rice cakes are reported to turn moderate in fructans from about 35 g (5 cakes), probably from processing.
Rice is on the low list of both Monash and FODMAP Friendly.

faq.a: Only a few. Sources differ, from 2 cakes to about 34 g, and larger amounts become moderate or high in fructans.
Sushi rice was below the fructan cut-off in a 2024 lab study. Watch the extras, like large amounts of avocado.

name: brown rice
answer: Yes. Monash's fibre guide lists 1 cup of cooked brown rice (180 g) as a low FODMAP serve, and it adds about 3 g of fibre. Brown rice holds a little more fructan than white rice in lab tests, but a normal bowl is still low.

disagreements.text: George Eats (August 2026) reports a much larger low amount for cooked brown rice: up to 500 g.

notes.text: In a 2024 study of cooked grains, brown rice had the most fructan of the rice types tested.
Brown rice is on Monash's list of whole grains it has tested and found low.
Brown rice flour is a different story: it's reported as moderate in fructans at 100 g.

faq.q: Is brown rice better than white rice for IBS?
faq.a: Both have low FODMAP serves. Brown rice has more fibre, which helps some people and bothers others, so a dietitian can help you choose.

faq.q: Is brown rice pasta low FODMAP?
faq.a: It's reported low up to about 421 g cooked, with moderate fructans in bigger serves.

name: quinoa
answer: Yes. Monash lists 1 cup of quinoa cooked in water (155 g) as a low FODMAP serve, with about 3 g of fibre. Quinoa flakes, flour and pasta were also tested low, so it's a handy swap for couscous or bulgur.

disagreements.text: George Eats (August 2026) reports much larger low amounts: up to 500 g for white and black quinoa and 421 g for red quinoa, which turns moderate in fructans from 422 g.

notes.text: Monash's list of whole grains tested low includes quinoa grain, flakes, flour and pasta.
Monash's wheat-swap table suggests 1 cup of quinoa flakes or 1 cup of quinoa pasta.
Monash suggests rinsing quinoa, then simmering it for 10 to 12 minutes.

faq.a: Using quinoa instead of bulgur is a common low FODMAP version. Check the rest of the salad, especially any onion.
It's reported to have a slightly smaller upper limit than white or black quinoa, but a normal 1 cup serve is fine on the published data.

name: wheat pasta
answer: Only a small bowl. Monash rates ½ cup of cooked wheat pasta (74 g) low, but a full serve, twice that, is rated high in fructans. Gluten-free or quinoa pasta, at about 1 cup, lets you eat a normal plate.

servings.note: Monash rates a full serve (twice this half-cup) as high, without printing the grams.

notes.text: FODMAP Friendly also says ½ cup of wheat pasta is low enough in fructans to count as low.
Wheat pasta is on Monash's list of high FODMAP grains at a usual serve, and it's one of the foods used to test fructans in the reintroduction step.
Monash's swap table suggests 1 cup of gluten-free or quinoa pasta instead.

faq.a: Usually, and Monash suggests a 1 cup serve. Check the label, because some gluten-free products use soy or legume flours, which are higher.

faq.q: Can I just eat less regular pasta?
faq.a: Yes. Half a cup cooked is low, so a small side of wheat pasta works during the elimination phase.

name: buckwheat
answer: Yes. Monash lists ¾ cup of cooked buckwheat groats (135 g) as a low FODMAP serve, giving about 7 g of fibre. Despite the name it isn't wheat, and buckwheat flour is reported low at 100 g.

disagreements.text: For buckwheat flour, Monash gives no upper limit, while the FODMAP Friendly app is reported to list it low up to 143 g.

notes.text: Monash's list of whole grains tested low includes buckwheat kernels and flour.
In a 2024 lab study, white and roasted buckwheat groats were both below the 0.3 g fructan cut-off per serve.

faq.q: Is buckwheat a kind of wheat?
faq.a: No. Despite the name, buckwheat isn't wheat, and Monash lists it among low FODMAP grains with a generous serve.
Buckwheat flour itself is low at 100 g. Check the rest of the recipe: regular milk and wheat flour add FODMAPs.

name: couscous
answer: No, wheat couscous is high in fructans. In a 2024 lab study, a 50 g dry serve held about 1 g of fructans, over three times the low cut-off, and Monash and FODMAP Friendly both list couscous as high. Quinoa, rice or gluten-free couscous are swaps.

servings.note: Measured at 1.02 g of fructans per 50 g dry serve; the low cut-off is 0.3 g. No public low serve was found.

notes.text: In Monash's 2011 analysis of 55 grain foods, couscous had the most fructan per portion, 1.12 g.
Monash uses wheat couscous as one of its test foods for fructans in the reintroduction step.
Monash's shopping list includes gluten-free couscous among low FODMAP grains; check its ingredients first.

faq.a: It's also made from wheat, so expect it to behave like regular couscous. No public lab result exists for it.

faq.q: How much couscous can I have?
faq.a: No low serve has been published. A 50 g dry portion was already well above the fructan cut-off in testing.

name: barley
answer: Mostly no. Monash groups barley with wheat and rye as high-fructan grains, and its lab rated plain barley grain red. Sprouting changed that: sprouted barley tested low. Some sites report a tiny low serve of cooked pearl barley, but we couldn't verify it.

servings.note: No verified gram figures. Monash rates a standard serve of barley high in fructans.

disagreements.text: A FODMAP Everyday page is reported to list ⅛ cup (28 g) of cooked pearl barley as low. We only saw this in a search result and couldn't open the page.

notes.text: When Monash sprouted barley grain, its FODMAP content fell enough to change the rating from red to green.
An NHS low FODMAP diet sheet lists pearl barley as a food to avoid but sprouted pearl barley as a suitable alternative.
A 2024 lab study found fine pearl barley groats second only to couscous for fructan among the grains it tested.

faq.a: Usually not. A bowl holds far more barley than the small serve some sites report. Rice or sprouted barley are lower-FODMAP options.
No, barley contains gluten. On a low FODMAP diet the issue is its fructans, not the gluten.

name: corn tortillas
answer: Yes. Monash has tested corn tortillas and lists them low. George Eats, citing Monash's figures as of August 2026, puts tortillas with added gum or fibre low up to 133 g (about 5½ tortillas), with moderate fructans above that. Older guides said 2 to 3 tortillas.

servings.form: corn tortillas, with added gum or fibre
servings.note: This is a reported upper low amount, not the older standard serve of 2 tortillas.

servings.form: corn tortillas, no added gum or fibre

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen (2024) lists 2 tortillas as low with added gum or fibre and 3 tortillas without. Other sites give these as 47 g and 57 g.

notes.text: Corn tortilla is on Monash's list of whole grain foods it has tested and found low.
Monash suggests corn tortillas for wraps, sandwiches and pizza bases.
Blue corn tortillas are reported low up to 370 g, with moderate GOS and fructans in larger amounts.

faq.q: Are hard taco shells low FODMAP?
faq.a: Hard corn taco shells are reported low even in large amounts. The fillings, like seasoning mixes with garlic or onion, are the bigger risk.
Wheat flour tortillas aren't covered by this data. Wheat breads are high at usual serves, so corn is the usual swap.

name: millet
answer: Yes. Monash has tested millet grain and flour and lists both as low FODMAP, though it hasn't published the grain's serve in grams on its website. Millet flour is reported low at 100 g (⅔ cup).

servings.note: No FODMAP group is named for millet; fructans are shown as the usual grain FODMAP.

notes.text: Monash's list of whole grains tested low includes millet grain and millet flour.
Monash suggests boiling millet for about 15 minutes, then draining and rinsing it, for salads or porridge.
An NHS low FODMAP diet sheet lists millet among suitable grains.

faq.a: Yes. Cooked millet has a similar small-grain feel, and unlike wheat couscous it's a tested low FODMAP grain.

faq.q: How much cooked millet is low FODMAP?
faq.a: Monash lists it as low but its public pages don't give the grams. Some sites say 1 cup cooked; we couldn't confirm that.

name: bulgur
answer: In small amounts. Monash lists ¼ cup of bulgur (44 g, uncooked weight) as a low FODMAP serve, and a full serve, about 88 g, is high in GOS and fructans. That's enough for a light tabbouleh, not a big bowl.

disagreements.text: Monash labels the 44 g serve as uncooked bulgur. George Eats and other sites give 44 g without saying whether it's cooked or dry.

notes.text: Monash describes bourghal as parboiled cracked wheat that is high in oligosaccharides at a full serve but low at half a serve.
A 2024 lab study found less fructan in cooked bulgur than in other wheat groats, which the authors link to heat during processing.
Monash suggests soaking bulgur in boiling water for about 30 minutes, or boiling it for about 12 minutes.

faq.a: It can be, if each portion has no more than ¼ cup (44 g) of dry bulgur and no onion. Quinoa is a common swap for a bigger serve.

faq.q: Is bulgur the same as couscous?
faq.a: Both are wheat, but bulgur has a tested low serve and couscous doesn't. Bulgur also tested lower in fructan.

name: pita bread
answer: Probably not at a full pita. No lab has published a pita result, but pita is a wheat bread, and Monash rates wheat bread low only at about one slice (24 g). An NHS diet sheet lists pitta bread with foods to avoid. Gluten-free pita is the swap.

estimateAnswer.line: Not lab-tested. Pita is wheat bread, and wheat bread is low only at about 1 slice (24 g).

servings.note: Not lab-tested. Estimated from its ingredients. Based on wheat bread data.

notes.text: Wheat bread is on the high list of both Monash and FODMAP Friendly at a usual serve.
FODMAP Friendly says one slice of wholemeal bread is low but two slices are high.
The NHS diet sheet suggests wheat-free or gluten-free pitta bread instead.

faq.q: How much pita can I eat?
faq.a: There's no tested amount. Going by wheat bread, a piece about the weight of one slice (24 g) is the closest guide.
Not for FODMAPs. Wholemeal wheat bread has the same small low serve as white.

name: za'atar
answer: Not tested as a blend. Za'atar is mostly dried herbs, sumac and sesame. Monash's shopping list includes dried herbs, most spices and sesame seeds, and a sprinkle uses very little, but no lab has published a serve. Check blends for garlic or onion.

estimateAnswer.line: No lab has tested the blend. Herbs and sesame are on Monash's low list; sumac has no public serve.

servings.note: Not lab-tested. Estimated from its ingredients.

notes.text: Sesame seeds are reported low up to 51 g, far more than a sprinkle of za'atar holds.
Monash's shopping list names dried and fresh herbs, and most spices except garlic and onion, as low FODMAP staples.

faq.a: The topping is a small amount, but the flatbread is usually wheat, which has only a small low serve.

faq.q: Can I make my own za'atar?
faq.a: Yes. Mixing dried thyme, sesame seeds and sumac yourself lets you skip any garlic or onion powder.

name: sumac
answer: No public lab number. Monash's shopping list counts most spices as low FODMAP, apart from garlic and onion, and sumac is used by the pinch. But we found no published sumac serve, so it counts as untested here.

estimateAnswer.line: No public lab serve. Monash counts most spices as low, but hasn't published sumac.

servings.note: Not lab-tested. Estimated from its ingredients. The FODMAP group is unknown; fructans are shown as a placeholder.

disagreements.text: A FODMAP Everyday recipe is reported to say Monash has lab-tested sumac. We couldn't open that page, and no gram serve is public.

notes.text: Monash's shopping list names most spices, except garlic and onion, as low FODMAP staples.

faq.a: Sumac gives a tangy, lemony taste rather than onion flavour. For onion taste, onion- or garlic-infused oil fits better.

faq.q: Is sumac the same as za'atar?
faq.a: No. Sumac is one spice; za'atar is a blend that usually includes sumac with herbs and sesame.

name: falafel
answer: Probably not, as usually made. Falafel uses soaked dried chickpeas or fava beans, not canned ones. Soaked, boiled chickpeas are low only at about 29 g, fava beans have no Monash low serve, and most packaged falafel also contains onion.

estimateAnswer.line: Not lab-tested. Soaked chickpeas or fava beans, plus onion in most packaged falafel.

servings.note: Not lab-tested. Estimated from its ingredients.

notes.text: Canned chickpeas have a bigger low serve, ¼ cup (42 g), because GOS leach into the can liquid.
Low FODMAP falafel recipes use canned chickpeas or edamame and suggest 3 to 4 pieces per person.
Chickpea flour, often used to bind falafel, is reported high in small serves.

faq.q: How many falafel can I eat?
faq.a: There's no lab-tested amount for falafel. Dietitian recipes made with canned chickpeas or edamame suggest 3 to 4 pieces per person.

faq.q: Is a falafel wrap low FODMAP?
faq.a: Probably not: the falafel and a wheat wrap or pita both add FODMAPs. A small homemade batch in a corn tortilla is a lower option.

name: halloumi
answer: Yes, in a small serve. Karlijn's Kitchen, citing Monash, and an NHS diet sheet both put halloumi low at 40 g (about 2 slices). Karlijn's Kitchen adds moderate lactose from 60 g and high from about 220 g. Monash calls haloumi a moderate-lactose cheese.

servings.note: Grams come from secondary sources; Monash's public pages give the rating but not the weights.

notes.text: Monash's FAQ lists haloumi with cream cheese and ricotta as cheeses with moderate amounts of lactose.
Karlijn's Kitchen found about 2 g of lactose per 100 g on the halloumi pack she checked.
An NHS diet sheet suggests limiting halloumi to 2 slices (40 g).

faq.q: Is halloumi lower in lactose than feta?
faq.a: No, feta has less. Monash measured just 0.13 g of lactose in 125 g of feta, while halloumi turns moderate from 60 g.
Only if you don't digest lactose well. Many people test this during the reintroduction step.

name: labneh
answer: Not tested. Labneh is yogurt strained until thick. Straining drains some whey, but no lab has published labneh's lactose level. Regular Greek yogurt, also strained, is low only at about 23 g, so keep portions small or make it from lactose-free yogurt.

estimateAnswer.line: No lab has tested labneh. Greek yogurt, also strained, is low only at about 23 g.

servings.note: Not lab-tested. Estimated from its ingredients.

notes.text: Regular-fat Greek yogurt is reported low at 23 g and moderate in lactose from 93 g.
Monash rates a 170 g serve of natural yogurt high in lactose.
Lactose-free plain yogurt is reported low up to 500 g.

faq.q: Can I make labneh from lactose-free yogurt?
faq.a: Yes. Straining lactose-free yogurt the same way gives a thick spread without the lactose question.

faq.q: Is labneh lower in lactose than yogurt?
faq.a: Probably somewhat, since some whey drains away, but nobody has published a lab number for it.

name: freekeh
answer: Probably not. No lab has published a FODMAP result for freekeh, which is made from young wheat, and an NHS low FODMAP diet sheet puts it with barley and rye on the avoid list. Rice, quinoa and millet are tested swaps.

estimateAnswer.line: No public lab number. An NHS diet sheet lists freekeh with barley and rye to avoid.

servings.note: Not lab-tested. Estimated from its ingredients.

notes.text: Monash mentions freekeh among grain foods but doesn't include it in its list of grains tested low.
Bulgur, another wheat grain, has a measured low serve of ¼ cup (44 g) uncooked.

faq.q: Is freekeh lower in FODMAPs than bulgur?
faq.a: Unknown: nobody has published a test. Bulgur at least has a measured low serve of ¼ cup (44 g) uncooked.
We'd count it as probably high until it's tested. A rice or quinoa version is the lower-FODMAP option.

name: ful medames
answer: Probably not. Ful medames is a stew of fava (broad) beans, and Monash has no low FODMAP serve for broad beans. FODMAP Friendly is reported to allow only about 21 g. The dish itself has not been lab-tested.

estimateAnswer.line: Not lab-tested. It's mostly fava beans, which have no low serve in Monash's data.
